meta.out_of_scope_guard: evaluator_test/ and data archives were never opened; no web access; no model inference; no new model fits. OCR statements come from the prior tesseract audit (analysis/instructions_review/IMAGE_OCR_REVIEW.md); this agent did not visually inspect images and makes no human-inspection claim.

requirements.title: Investigate the actual raw files instead of assuming uniformity
requirements.requirement: Verify trip organisation, file naming, row counts, data types and column meanings; do not assume every trip is identical or that a GPS row corresponds to a network row.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Dataset audit manifest covering every trip and file (counts, sizes, dtypes), plus report §2.2 answers.
requirements.status_note: analysis/data_audit/ (manifest.csv, per_trip.csv, summary.json) and the phase-three PDF; refresh only if inputs change before final submission.

requirements.title: Honour documented raw file formats (.track/.nodes/.arcs/.route)
requirements.requirement: 3-column whitespace .track (lon, lat, ts seconds, ~1 Hz), 2-column .nodes, integer from/to .arcs (row index = arc_id), 1-column .route of chronological ground-truth arc_ids.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Parsers read exactly these formats; .route treated as arc sequence, not per-observation labels.
requirements.status_note: Implemented; proxy observation labels derived from route geometry are disclosed as such in DEVELOPMENT_PROVENANCE.md and the report.

requirements.title: Structured initial EDA covering all listed items
requirements.requirement: Identify trips per partition, observations per trip, file availability/sizes, types/columns, missing or invalid GPS, timestamp ordering and gaps, geographic extent, network nodes/segments, connectivity, isolated nodes/disconnected components, anomalous trips, reference-route availability and structure.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: EDA outputs and report §2.2 addressing each item; partition named per analysis.
requirements.status_note: Covered by data audit + phase-three report; final-five PDF must carry it forward.

requirements.title: Geographically appropriate distance computations
requirements.requirement: Justify projected CRS or geodesic distance (degrees-Euclidean is not physical distance), check coordinate order and plausibility, account for noise/gaps/irregular timestamps.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Report states the distance computation used and why it fits the dataset scale.
requirements.status_note: Geodesic/projected handling documented in the phase-three report.

requirements.title: Treat reference routes as reference, not error-free ground truth
requirements.requirement: Do not assume supplied routes are independently verified physical truth; identify limitations, state assumptions, avoid overstating label certainty.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Report and provenance state the limitation; metrics derived from route-derived labels labelled as proxy.
requirements.status_note: Proxy-label disclosure present in DEVELOPMENT_PROVENANCE.md and report; keep in the final-five PDF.

requirements.title: Honour the 80/10/10 partition scheme
requirements.requirement: 80 training trips for fitting/development/CV/optimisation; 10 student-testing trips for development-stage comparison; 10 evaluator-testing trips for final evaluation only.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Protocol files and code show the split; no evaluator trip in any training artefact.
requirements.status_note: Grouped TRAIN CV + student-test evaluation used throughout phase three.

requirements.title: Leakage-prevention rules
requirements.requirement: No trip split across partitions; evaluator data not used for training, feature selection, algorithm or hyperparameter choice; no manual alteration from known routes; no hardcoded answers; preprocessing fitted on permitted training data only; evaluator ground truth kept out of the pipeline.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Code review + freeze records show TRAIN-only fitting; evaluator inputs untouched.
requirements.status_note: Evaluator_test/ never opened by this audit or (per records) by the pipeline; maintain at final freeze.

requirements.title: Retain exploration evidence
requirements.requirement: Dataset inventory, summary statistics, coordinate/pattern plots, interactive Folium maps, network size/connectivity tables, data-quality record.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Artifacts committed in the repository.
requirements.status_note: Present in repo and phase-three report figures.

requirements.title: Team can explain dataset organisation, relations, quality concerns, assumptions
requirements.requirement: At the end of exploration each team should be able to explain how the raw dataset is organised, what each file represents, how components relate, quality concerns and assumptions.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Written answers exist (done); a human can answer viva questions on them (not verifiable by AI).
requirements.status_note: Documented evidence exists; the explanation ability itself belongs to the human team at viva. Disclose; do not fake.

requirements.title: At least FIVE distinct models trained, evaluated and compared before selection
requirements.requirement: Verbatim: 'Teams must train and evaluate at leastFIVE different models before selecting their final model.' Selection must be supported by experimental results, performance comparisons and technical reasoning; direct selection without meaningful experiments incurs deductions.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Final report table with all five models (LR, KNN/distance-weighted, Bagging, GaussianNB, HistGradientBoosting), each with TRAIN grouped-CV and student-test metrics from actual runs, plus per-model subsections.
requirements.status_note: LR/KNN/Bagging complete under the phase-three protocol. GaussianNB and HistGradientBoosting historical all-80 artifacts exist with all-ten predictions and are being validity/identity-audited by the model-audit child (d868726d). The consolidated five-model comparison and final selection are not yet produced. Do not publish a five-model claim before the final-five evidence exists.

requirements.title: Multiple algorithm families
requirements.requirement: Students are strongly encouraged to explore models from multiple algorithm families; the family table is examples and suggestions, not a fixed list.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Five final families span the encouraged table: linear/probabilistic (LR, GNB), instance-based (distance-weighted KNN), ensemble (Bagging), boosting (HistGB).
requirements.status_note: The latest user scope makes five families explicit, which satisfies this encouraged item and the mandatory five-model rule together. Three families frozen; two pending final-five consolidation.

requirements.title: Experimental-design rules for every model
requirements.requirement: Train >=5 distinct models; record each configuration; fit and cross-validate on the 80 training trips; compare on the ten student-testing trips; apply preprocessing consistently; avoid training-accuracy-only selection; record training and inference time where practical; retain logs, seeds, configurations and results.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Per-model config records, seeds, timing and result files for all five families under the final protocol.
requirements.status_note: Complete for the three-family phase; the final-five run must extend the same records to GaussianNB and HistGradientBoosting (or adopt their audited artifacts) before consolidation.

requirements.title: Evaluation-metric set and primary-metric justification
requirements.requirement: Report, where applicable: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, confusion matrix, log loss, observation-level Top-1 accuracy, candidate miss rate, route continuity, sequence-level performance, training and inference time; explain the primary selection metric and why it is appropriate.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Metric tables per model; primary-metric justification paragraph in the report.
requirements.status_note: Done for the three frozen families; extend to all five, including log loss for the probabilistic models (GNB, LR) where applicable and stated N/A with reasons elsewhere.

requirements.title: Comparison identifies the listed per-model facts
requirements.requirement: Comparison must identify model name, algorithm family, important configuration, training/CV performance, student-testing performance, precision, recall, F1, log loss where applicable, computational efficiency, route continuity.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: The consolidated report table (see R-DL-05) filled for all five models from actual results.
requirements.status_note: Phase-three table covers three families; five-family table outstanding.

requirements.title: Selection considerations including generalisation; never training accuracy alone
requirements.requirement: Selection must consider generalisation performance, stability across validation folds, probability quality, inference speed, model complexity, decoder compatibility; 'Do not select a model solely because it achieves high training accuracy.'
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Selection rationale in the final report referencing measured CV-vs-student-test behaviour and fold stability for all five candidates.
requirements.status_note: Done for the three-family selection (TRAIN-only CV, documented generalisation gap analysis). The final five-family selection must repeat this before the model freeze.

requirements.title: Bayesian hyperparameter optimisation protocol
requirements.requirement: After the initial comparison, run a Bayesian search on a promising model: justified search space, stated objective, group-aware CV on the 80 training trips, recorded trials, best configuration, refit, evaluation on the ten student-testing trips, tuned-vs-untuned comparison, reported computational cost.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Search configs, trial log (search_results.jsonl), objective CSV, best values, tuned-vs-untuned metric comparison on identical partitions, cost statement.
requirements.status_note: Bagging 8-trial TRAIN-only Bayesian search is complete and frozen (reports/phase_three/decoder/search_*). A historical TRAIN-only HistGB 12-trial search exists and the model-audit child must verify its full trial study before any reuse. If the final five-family selection picks a different model than an already-searched one, a fresh Bayesian search for that model is required before the final report.

requirements.title: Evaluator partition excluded from every optimisation choice
requirements.requirement: The evaluator-testing partition must not be used to choose the search space, objective, hyperparameters, model or thresholds.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: All search records reference TRAIN grouped CV only; no evaluator artifacts in any search input.
requirements.status_note: Upheld so far; re-verify at the final freeze, including the deferred evaluator website section.

requirements.title: HMM route reconstruction driven by the selected model's outputs
requirements.requirement: Route reconstruction should use the selected model's outputs consistently; sequential information plus network connectivity produce a coherent route.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Decoder consumes the frozen final classifier's probabilities; no independent hand-tuned matcher.
requirements.status_note: True for the frozen Bagging model. The final decoder must be re-frozen against whichever model wins the five-family comparison.

requirements.title: Required route-reconstruction experiments (incl. classifier-only negative control)
requirements.requirement: Describe hidden states; preserve candidate-to-segment correspondence; explain emission and transition modelling; explain the Viterbi recurrence; handle missing candidates and invalid transitions; handle GPS gaps; return a predicted segment per relevant observation; compare classifier-only with classifier-plus-HMM predictions (the negative control); report pointwise and sequence-level performance; analyse route continuity.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Ablation artifacts (classifier-only vs classifier+HMM) on student data, per-observation assignments, continuity metrics, and report §5 answers.
requirements.status_note: Phase-three ablation exists (reports/phase_three/decoder/ablation_run.json, student_ablation.*). Must be re-run or re-verified for the final five-family winner before the final report.

requirements.title: Decoder parameters optimised on training/student data only
requirements.requirement: Optimise decoder parameters using training and student-testing data only.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Decoder calibration records reference permitted partitions only.
requirements.status_note: Phase-three calibration used permitted data; repeat the check at the final freeze.

requirements.title: Nine required components
requirements.requirement: Data-processing implementation, model-experimentation implementation, Bayesian-optimisation implementation, HMM/Viterbi implementation, API (FastAPI), UI, model and configuration artifacts, technical report, GitHub repository.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Each component present and cross-referenced in the repository and report.
requirements.status_note: All exist from phase three; final-five updates flow into the same components.

requirements.title: Two-laptop deployment architecture
requirements.requirement: Laptop 1 hosts the trained classifier, HMM/Viterbi, road-network information and server-side evaluation; Laptop 2 displays the ten evaluation-trip options, sends the selection to the API and shows the returned route and results. Final-evaluation steps 1-9 run API on Laptop 1 and UI on Laptop 2.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Per the brief: a live two-laptop demonstration at evaluation. Replacement evidence per user instruction: public same-origin deployment at https://ml.d3va.dev with API bound to loopback, reference data server-private, UI/API served through a Cloudflare tunnel from this computer.
requirements.status_note: The user explicitly replaced the separate-UI-laptop requirement with the public website; the site is deployed and verified. If organisers insist on the literal two-laptop setup at the venue, humans must set up and demonstrate it: that part is a human_external_blocker. Disclose the substitution in the report rather than implying the original architecture was used.

requirements.title: Ten reserved evaluation trips selectable and scored end-to-end
requirements.requirement: The UI displays the ten reserved trips; evaluator selects any one; UI sends the trip ID; the API runs the complete prediction pipeline and computes accuracy from its internal reference data; UI displays route and results. Must work for all ten, not one demo example.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Evaluator-section implementation supporting an evaluator root without code changes; all-ten run recorded after the final model/decoder freeze.
requirements.status_note: Human reported ten new evaluator trips last task; current full scope handles this AFTER the final model/decoder freeze. Inputs under evaluator_test/ were not read and must not be read before the freeze.

requirements.title: Ground truth stays server-side; no hardcoding or API bypass
requirements.requirement: Ground-truth labels must remain server-side and never be exposed to the prediction model or UI; hardcoded outputs and bypassing the API are not permitted; repositories will be examined.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Architecture review: reference data private to the server; no evaluator labels in UI bundle or model inputs; no hardcoded trip answers in code.
requirements.status_note: Held in the current deployment; re-verify after the OpenCode website rebuild and final freeze.

requirements.title: Show the evaluator the API request logs
requirements.requirement: Students are required to show the evaluator the API logs on the laptop receiving the inference requests, on the endpoint.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Persisted, presentable request logs for the evaluator session; in the replacement deployment, receiving-terminal service events for real HTTPS match requests.
requirements.status_note: Phase-three delivery verification reconciled ten real HTTPS requests with CLI route geometry. After the final freeze and OpenCode website, regenerate and keep the logs for the evaluation session.

requirements.title: Deliverable 1: public GitHub repository with eleven required components
requirements.requirement: Repository contains data processing, feature engineering, model training (every model experimented with), model evaluation, hyperparameter optimisation, HMM and Viterbi, API, UI, deployment configuration, visualisations (Folium map generation), and supporting results (CSVs, logs, configs, summaries).
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Public repo (github.com/DevaOnL/ML-Hackathon) with all components; final-five additions merged.
requirements.status_note: PR #5 merged to main covers the three-family phase. The five-family, OpenCode-website and final-report updates still need a later merge.

requirements.title: Repository rules
requirements.requirement: All source committed (not only the final model); saved weights and configs subject to size constraints; README with installation, execution and deployment instructions; clearly named folders; accessible to evaluators; no secrets committed.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Repo audit: README, folder layout, included artifacts, secret scan clean.
requirements.status_note: Held in main; re-run the secret scan before the final merge.

requirements.title: Deliverable 2: one consolidated PDF report
requirements.requirement: One consolidated PDF per team, following the required structure, with actual experimental results, tables, graphs and geographical visualisations; every reported result verifiable from the repository; no separate per-model reports.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Final PDF regenerated after the five-family freeze; report facts traceable to repo artifacts (checked evidence facts).
requirements.status_note: The 23-page phase-three PDF is complete and verified. The final five-family PDF does not exist yet and must be regenerated after the model/decoder freeze and the OpenCode website work.

requirements.title: Report §2.2 dataset understanding and EDA
requirements.requirement: Answer how the data was preprocessed and what patterns were observed; which features were extracted and why; include missing-value analysis, GPS trajectory plots, road-network visualisations, at least one Folium map; clearly mention which partition each analysis used.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Report section with the listed items and partition labels.
requirements.status_note: Present in the phase-three PDF; carry forward into the final report.

requirements.title: Report §3.1 consolidated comparison table with >=5 models
requirements.requirement: Table columns exactly: Model, Algorithm Family, Key Configuration, CV Macro F1-score, Top-1 Accuracy, Route continuity, Student-Test Macro F1-score, Log Loss, Inference Time; actual results; N/A cells explained.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Five filled rows (LR, KNN, Bagging, GaussianNB, HistGB) from actual runs under one protocol.
requirements.status_note: Three rows exist from phase three; the five-row final table waits on the GNB/HistGB final-five audit results.

requirements.title: Report §3.2 compulsory per-model questions
requirements.requirement: For every model: why the algorithm suits PathSnap; strengths and limitations; important hyperparameters and initial values; loss function or optimisation objective; student-testing performance; observation-level Top-1, Macro F1 and Log Loss where applicable; overfitting/underfitting with supporting evidence. No textbook-only answers.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Five per-model subsections with measured numbers and behaviour tied to actual experiments.
requirements.status_note: Done for three families; GaussianNB and HistGradientBoosting subsections outstanding.

requirements.title: Report §3.3 compulsory model visualisations
requirements.requirement: CV Macro F1 comparison across all models; student-testing Top-1 and Macro F1 comparisons; Log Loss comparison where applicable; confusion matrices optional; training and validation loss plots only for models producing epoch-wise training histories; every graph from actual results; model-comparison plots justifying selection; no artificial training curves.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Chart set covering all five models, generated from actual result files, with a stated N/A explanation for epoch-wise loss plots where the family produces no training history.
requirements.status_note: Charts exist for three families. LR, KNN, Bagging, GaussianNB and HistGB (as currently used) do not produce epoch-wise training histories, so loss plots are conditional N/A; do not fabricate learning curves. The comparison charts must be regenerated for all five before the final build.

requirements.title: Report §4 Bayesian optimisation section
requirements.requirement: State hyperparameters searched, ranges or distributions, objective function, trial count, best values, tuned-vs-untuned comparison on CV Macro F1, student Top-1, student Macro F1, Log Loss where applicable, and inference time, using the same metrics and partitions for both.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Section backed by search configs, trial log and a like-for-like tuned/untuned metric table for the final selected model.
requirements.status_note: Complete for Bagging. If the five-family winner differs, run and document its search (see R-MT-07).

requirements.title: Report §5 HMM/Viterbi section with improvement evidence
requirements.requirement: Explain hidden states, emission and transition calculation, missing candidates and GPS gaps, disconnected-segment handling; whether HMM decoding improved the route, supported by experimental results; compare classifier-only vs classifier-plus-HMM; discuss cases where decoding did not help.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Section plus ablation numbers for the final model.
requirements.status_note: Written for the phase-three model; refresh against the final five-family winner.

requirements.title: Report §6 Folium geographical visualisation
requirements.requirement: Mandatory Folium maps from the team's actual implementation showing GPS observations, road-network geometry, reference route where available, and predicted route; distinguishable colours/markers, labels or legend, appropriate extent and zoom, comparability, layer controls; at least one map screenshot/export in the PDF; interactive HTML or generator code in the repo; no unrelated or fabricated maps.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Maps in the final PDF plus committed HTML/generation code.
requirements.status_note: Present from phase three; regenerate the predicted-route layers for the final model and the OpenCode site.

requirements.title: Report §7 API, UI and deployment evidence
requirements.requirement: Screenshots of the working UI; screenshots of successful API responses on the CMD of the receiving laptop; submitted source must match the demonstrated implementation.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Final report carries UI screenshots and captured API responses from the final deployment (the OpenCode-themed site), and the demonstrated source equals the submitted source.
requirements.status_note: Phase-three screenshots exist, but the user ordered the OpenCode website with the kind theme only after all five models are trained and tested; §7 evidence must be re-captured from that final site.

requirements.title: Report §8 academic-integrity acknowledgement
requirements.requirement: Reports and GitHub submissions face integrity checks: plagiarism checks on content, cross-team comparison of code/configs/weights/results, verification of reported metrics against actual outputs, technical questioning; the report must represent the team's actual work; every member must be able to explain it.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Truthful report whose numbers are reproducible from the repo (mechanically verifiable) and a team able to defend it (human).
requirements.status_note: The mechanical part is upheld by policy (only measured results, AI assistance disclosed in DEVELOPMENT_PROVENANCE.md). The member-explanation and integrity-defence part belongs to the humans; disclose the AI-assisted provenance rather than claiming unaided human authorship.

requirements.title: First-phase evaluation before lunch break
requirements.requirement: Notice on the title table: 'There will be first phase evaluation before lunch break.'
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Team knows the event schedule and has a submission ready before the first-phase checkpoint.
requirements.status_note: The organisers' schedule is not in the workspace; the user must confirm when the first-phase evaluation happens. No date guessing.

requirements.title: Evidence of meaningful experimentation
requirements.requirement: Train and compare at least five models before selecting a final one; support selection with recorded results; explain strengths and limitations of the chosen approach; demonstrate Bayesian HPO; retain the search record; evaluate models and the decoder using permitted development data. Selecting without meaningful experimentation may cost marks.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Same as R-MT-01/03/07 plus the explanation in the report.
requirements.status_note: Three families fully evidenced; five-family evidence and the final selection rationale are pending.

requirements.title: Independent work; no inter-team sharing
requirements.requirement: Each team independently implements, trains, evaluates and selects its own models; sharing model files, weights, configurations, code, derived datasets or results between teams is prohibited; submissions are compared across teams and sections; teams must explain selection, implementation, training and results during evaluation.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: No inter-team transfer in the workspace record; development provenance disclosed; humans able to explain the work.
requirements.status_note: Nothing in the workspace indicates inter-team sharing; the work is AI-assisted at the owner's request and that is disclosed in docs/DEVELOPMENT_PROVENANCE.md with commit attribution kept honest. The during-evaluation explanation requirement is human. Do not claim human-only independent work.

requirements.title: Report authenticity
requirements.requirement: Prohibited: fabricating metrics, graphs or execution results; fabricating citations or implementation details; copying another team's report; submitting explanations the team cannot defend. Teams remain responsible for accuracy and originality of all content.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Every reported number traceable to a measured artifact; no invented plots or citations.
requirements.status_note: Held so far by policy (checked evidence facts in the phase-three PDF; proxy-label metrics explicitly labelled). Keep the same discipline through the final build; the AI-provenance disclosure stays in the submission.

requirements.title: Viva and demonstration topics
requirements.requirement: Organisers may ask team members to explain dataset structure, preprocessing, feature engineering, model comparisons and selection, Bayesian HPO, HMM implementation, Viterbi decoding, API, UI and experimental results; teams should demonstrate they understand and can reproduce their submitted work.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Each team member can answer questions on the listed topics and can reproduce the work from the repository.
requirements.status_note: No document states a five-member team; the rule binds 'every team member' regardless of size. An AI agent cannot make humans understand the material. Recommend the team schedule a walkthrough of the final report and a live reproduction run before evaluation.

requirements.title: Similarity review scope
requirements.requirement: Organisers compare source code, repository history, model architectures, weights, hyperparameter configurations, experimental results, reports, graphs and tables; similarity may trigger review; no single similarity measure is automatic proof of plagiarism.
requirements.acceptance_evidence: Nothing to produce; awareness that standard algorithms naturally resemble other teams' work.
requirements.status_note: Recorded for awareness; no action beyond honest provenance.
